title: Make a published on-call rota stay as it was published

blocks.text: The paging service keeps each team's current on-call `Rota` in a plain field, and the alert threads read it with no lock, many times a second. The admin UI builds a rota from the lists an admin is editing and, when the admin presses Publish, stores it in that field. Last Tuesday night the payments team's backup was paged instead of its primary: an admin had published the week's rota, then went on reordering Tuesday in the editor for next week's draft, without publishing again.

Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/OnCall.java`, the record's compact constructor. When you're done, a rota pages the people it was built with, in the order it was built with, for as long as it lives: whatever the editor does to its lists afterwards, and whatever a caller tries with the lists and the map the rota hands out. About four lines in total.
The tests build rotas from fresh mutable lists and maps, the way the editor does, and change them afterwards.

cases.says: a rota answers its team, each day's people, its escalation chain and the paging order it was built with
changing the escalation list or the week map the rota was built from, after building it, changes nothing in the rota
nothing the rota hands out, its lists or its map or a day's list in it, can be used to change it
changing one day's list after building the rota leaves that day's paging order as it was built

origin.section: Immutable Objects Need No Edge; Effectively Immutable Ones Need One Safe Publication

concepts: An object is immutable only if nothing it reaches can change after construction: a record keeping a caller's list, or an unmodifiable view of it, changes when the caller's list does, and nested collections need copies too.
